subject: Canary degradation — request for immediate fallback and version hold
messages:
From: Morgan Ellis <morgan@healthsync.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@healthsync.io>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Canary launch causing elevated p95 — need fallback

Hi Priya,

We just started the staged rollout you coordinated this morning and are already seeing tail latency spikes on our transaction endpoint. Over the last 20 minutes p95 has moved from ~180ms to ~420ms (our contract SLA is p95 < 200ms) and we’re seeing a small but growing error rate (0.6% to 1.8%). Traffic is largely production traffic; the window aligns with a regional spike.

We need Redwood to do one of the following immediately:
- Trigger an automated fallback to the previously pinned model (v2.1) for the next 30–60 minutes, or
- If auto-fallback is not available, manually pin traffic back to v2.1 and hold ramping until we complete a short triage.

Can you confirm steps you will take and an ETA? If you want us to pause client traffic, we can do that but prefer Redwood to handle the rollback so our users are uninterrupted.

Attaching a short snapshot of our trace IDs and a screen grab.

Thanks,
Morgan Ellis
Head of Platform
HealthSync

Attachment: healthsync-traces-20260527.png (image/png)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Ellis <morgan@healthsync.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Canary launch causing elevated p95 — need fallback

Hi Morgan — thanks for the quick heads-up and data. Sorry you hit this during the ramp. We’re taking ownership and will execute a conservative rollback path immediately. Plan below (I’ll keep this thread for audit):

1) Immediate (T+5): enable automatic canary escape hatch for the HealthSync route — policy: revert 100% of new-canary traffic to v2.1 if p95 > 250ms for two consecutive 1-minute buckets.
2) Short hold (T+10): pause further ramping and set canary max concurrent connections to the current baseline (throttle new sessions).
3) If auto-fallback triggers or we manually revert, we will hold on v2.1 for at least 60 minutes while we collect telemetry and root cause.
4) Post-mortem (T+4h): Redwood and HealthSync agree on next steps for remediation and a guarded re-roll.

Operational notes:
- I have CC’d Lauren (customer success lead) and Aditya (runtime ops) to authorize manual pin if auto-fallback does not engage.
- Attachment is our internal runbook snippet for canary escape hatch.
- Dashboard links: https://console.redwood.ai/canary/HS-041?range=1h and the HubSpot ticket is hubspot.com/deal/HS-2026-041.

Please confirm you’re OK with us taking the fallback. If you require a formal change order or legal sign-off, say so and we’ll get docs queued — but for user impact we recommend immediate fallback.

— Priya Natarajan
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai

I’ve enacted the first set of controls:
- Auto-fallback policy created and enabled for HS-041 (threshold p95 > 250ms × 2 consecutive mins).
- Canary ramp paused and new session intake throttled to baseline.
- If fallback doesn’t trigger in the next 5 minutes, I will perform a manual pin to v2.1 (will post audit event).

Dropping a telemetry snapshot to the thread — see attachment for the 09:10–09:30 window. I’m continuing to watch traces and error budgets.

— Aditya
Runtime Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Canary launch causing elevated p95 — need fallback

Thanks, Priya and Aditya — appreciate the rapid response and clear plan.

We saw the auto-fallback engage at ~09:35 and metrics returned to baseline; error rate dropped to 0.2% and p95 back around 190ms. Alicia and I are comfortable with holding on v2.1 while you triage.

Two requests as a follow-up:
1) Please add a short change note that we can use internally to tell ops teams what happened and the duration of the hold (we’ll send to our on-call rotation).
2) After the triage, can Redwood propose a guarded re-roll schedule (narrower ramp windows and a stricter fail-open threshold) so we can sign off and prevent recurrence?

If you need formal sign-off paperwork from procurement/legal for incident remediation credits or SLA exceptions, flag that and I’ll route it. Otherwise we’re good with the remediation path described.

Thanks again for the quick action.

— Morgan Ellis
Head of Platform, HealthSync
